item.description: Tage Thompson #72 of the Buffalo Sabres celebrates after scoring a goal during an NHL regular season game against the Anaheim Ducks on October 29, 2026 at Honda Center in Anaheim, California. item.title: Potential Yankees-David Bednar reunion’s importance draws honest opinions
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Potential Yankees-David Bednar reunion’s importance draws honest opinions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have several important decisions to make this offseason, but what they do with David Bednar is a major one. After bringing stability to the ninth inning, the closer has made a strong case for another season in the Bronx. Acquired from the Pittsburgh Pirates at the 2025 trade deadline, Bednar had to navigate early velocity concerns and criticism following blown saves before becoming a central figure in New York’s bullpen. Bednar converted 35 of 39 save opportunities in 2026, finishing with a 2.47 ERA and 76 strikeouts across 69.1 innings. He also delivered in the postseason, allowing no runs in three innings. His work helped settle a role that has often been a question mark for New York . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That production is why Bednar is a player the Yankees should prioritize re-signing . The Talkin’ Yankees show acknowledged the risks of committing multiple years to relievers, but argued that Bednar has earned the opportunity to remain the team’s bullpen anchor. There is evidence to support that view. Since joining New York in 2025, Bednar has recorded a 2.39 ERA and 45 saves over 94 innings. He continued to evolve this season, leaning more on his splitter and holding hitters to a .149 average in at-bats that ended with the pitch. His control improved, too, as he posted a career-best 7.1% walk rate. The biggest obstacle may be the cost. Bednar earned $9 million this season and is likely to attract interest from other teams. The Yankees could explore alternatives in free agency, but finding someone who can provide the same reliability will be difficult. With other bullpen decisions still looming, bringing Bednar back would give New York a proven closer and remove one major concern from its offseason checklist. item.title: Pleasant makes it four in a row at Utica's expense in volleyball
item.description: COLUMBUS — Pleasant continues to make it look easy. Yet to drop a set this season, the top-seeded Spartans continued that streak with a 3-0 victory over No. 4 seed Utica to win the Division V volleyball district championship Oct. 29 at Ohio Dominican University's Alumni Hall. It is Pleasant's fourth straight district title, and the victory puts them in the regional semifinals in the familiar O-rena at Ontario High School with a 6 p.m. start Wednesday, Nov. 4. The Spartans (25-0) will face Centerburg (23-2) after the third-seeded Trojans got by No. 7 North Union 3-1 in the first match at ODU Oct. 29. "We’re leaving everything out on the court. We know this is our last chance to do it. We haven’t done it the past two years (which is win a state championship)," Pleasant senior libero Kam Roberts said. "I think we’re hungry for it this year. We’re working hard for it in practice, and it’s really showing on the court." Fast start sets up the Spartans Pleasant jumped out to an 8-0 lead in the first set, bumping it to 13-2 and 19-5 before finishing it with a 25-10 victory. It set the tone for the night. "We really focus on bringing a lot of energy just so we can stay up and positive and get starts on teams so we can keep it going because momentum keeps going through the whole game," Pleasant senior setter Macy Hamper said. It's what coach Kory Ute wanted to see out of the Spartans. "We did better. We had a rough week at practice trying to put all the little pieces in place," Ute said. "It’s always important in a tournament situation that you try to get ahead because you’re going to have bumps along the way." item.title: 8 takeaways from Mizzou basketball’s final exhibition game, loss at UNLV
item.description: What happens in Vegas … Missouri basketball’s preseason ended with a 90-81 loss at the hands of UNLV on Thursday night in Las Vegas, as the Tigers surrendered a seven-point lead with a shocking start to the second half to fall in their final exhibition game. The Runnin’ Rebels outscored the Tigers 47-33 in the second half, and MU will head back to Columbia after splitting its public preseason games. The Tigers will officially open their new season Tuesday, Nov. 3, at Mizzou Arena with a game against Cleveland State. More: Missouri basketball drops exhibition game against UNLV to end preseason We’ve had our last look at Dennis Gates’ squad before the new year gets underway. Here are eight takeaways from Mizzou’s loss in Vegas: Jason Crowe Jr., you have our attention It was another tremendous night for the talented freshman. It looks a lot like he’s going to lead MU in scoring on more nights than he doesn’t. Crowe had a team-high 25 points, six assists and three steals in the exhibition loss — a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming night in Sin City. We’re not sure Crowe’s ever seen a shot he didn’t like. He scored at every level, knocking down a couple shots from deep, getting to the line for a game-high 14 free-throw attempts and attacking the paint every time he got an inch on a screen. Mizzou has a really exciting player running the point. Bryson Tiller had a poor preseason There is a lot to like about Bryson Tiller’s game, but it’s hard to see through the costly mistakes. He can definitely rebound, adding a team-high eight boards against UNLV. His handle for a big man is strong. His defense at the rim, especially against Kansas State, was extremely encouraging with five blocks. But he’s got the turnover bug right now, and some of his decisions on the offensive end were perplexing. He had five turnovers against the Wildcats. He had four in the opening six minutes — to go with three fouls in that same timespan — against UNLV, finishing the game with five. Mizzou had 20 turnovers, so this isn’t just a Tiller problem. But, he’s been the most giveaway-prone of the bunch. Tiller also finished the preseason 4-of-14 shooting from the field, which is 28.6% over two games. That also has to improve, given the range he’ll take most of his shot attempts. Will Mark Mitchell play a different role? We all know Mitchell can drive and draw fouls. item.title: Bayern and Kane host Dortmund after week of 'extremes'
item.description: Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane reacts after winning the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday. (FRANCK FIFE) Bayern Munich host long-time foes Borussia Dortmund on Saturday after a rollercoaster week punctuated by coach Vincent Kompany's hospitalisation and Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph. Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, a mainstay in Bayern's midfield, has missed three games on compassionate leave due to the sudden death of his father. Luis Diaz, Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Aleksander Pavlovic have all battled injury for the defending champions. Bayern's issues have pushed what is usually the biggest match of the Bundesliga season into the background. The only unbeaten teams after seven matchdays, Bayern and Dortmund sit level on points, with Saturday's hosts ahead on goal difference. Dortmund coach Niko Kovac said Thursday his side, who have also battled injury issues this season, were "getting closer" to Bayern. But Bayern's main task will be to shut out the noise and focus on the game. - 'Highs and the lows' - After showing signs of illness in Bayern's 6-1 thumping of RB Leipzig, Kompany returned to the dugout for last week's 2-2 home draw with Arsenal, but collapsed on the training pitch two days later. Later diagnosed with meningeal irritation, the Belgian was released after five days in hospital on Wednesday, but Bayern said it will likely be "weeks, not days" until he returns to work. Charged with carrying Kompany's clipboard, assistant Aaron Danks hoped the waves of emotion would galvanise the side. "You've seen the full extremes of life in the last week. The joys and highs for Harry, and the lows of some of the things we've had to go through in the last seven days," Danks said Tuesday. "Internally we have to find a balance... In these moments, you understand the human being is the most important thing... "These moments do bring you closer, because they're challenging moments, but to get through these moments we've had to rely on our team spirit and our togetherness." At the other end of the emotional spectrum is Kane, who received the game's highest individual honour on Monday. Kane said Wednesday it had been a "crazy week" for himself and the club, adding: "I get quite embarrassed by it, but I know it's a big deal. "It's been a whirlwind 48 hours, it's nice to be back here and feel at home again." Kane became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 and just the fifth ever to win the Ballon d'Or, with some calling for the England captain to be knighted. item.title: Jorge Martin declared fit to race in Malaysian GP after FP1
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin has received the necessary medical clearances to take part in the remainder of the Malaysian Grand Prix after the opening practice on Friday. Having been initially declared fit by MotoGP’s official doctor Angel Charte on Thursday, the Aprilia rider needed to undergo further evaluation after the first track session of the weekend before being allowed to continue at Sepang. As the timer to FP1 ran out, Charte was already in the Aprilia garage to assess the right wrist the Spaniard broke in his crash at the Phillip Island sprint last Saturday. Having been satisfied with his condition, Charte gave Martin the all-clear to race at Sepang and keep his title hopes alive. In a short statement issued around midday, less than half an hour after FP1 ended, Aprilia noted that “Jorge Martin has been declared fit to race at the Malaysian GP”. While Martin has been given the green-light to race, he faces a significant challenge in closing the gap to the front after finishing 20th in FP1, 1.8s off the best time set by his title rival Marc Marquez on the factory Ducati. Martin’s team-mate Marco Bezzecchi finished second on the timesheets, albeit 0.474s down on Marquez. Heading into this weekend’s Malaysian GP, Marquez holds a 10-point lead in the standings over Martin, with Bezzecchi 50 points down in third. Fernandez withdraws from Malaysian GP Raul Fernandez, Trackhouse Racing Raul Fernandez, Trackhouse Racing While Martin has been declared fit to race, Aprilia will be down to three riders this weekend after Trackhouse’s Raul Fernandez withdrew from the weekend due to his own injury. The 26-year-old completed just two laps of the Sepang International Circuit in FP1 before pulling into the pits with visible pain. The Spaniard had been nursing a finger injury that he sustained during the sprint race at the Indonesian Grand Prix earlier this month. Although he went on to complete the Mandalika weekend, finishing second to Bezzecchi in the full-distance race, his problems worsened at Phillip Island last weekend and he was forced to retire early from the sprint race. After being declared unfit to take part in the Australian GP, which was ultimately cancelled, Fernandez travelled to Malaysia with the aim of racing again. However, after reporting severe pain while riding the bike, he took the decision to cut short his weekend and focus on his recovery. item.description: To compete in Deaf Rugby, players must have a hearing loss of at least 40 decibels in both ears. [John Fraser-Natale] Wales men and women are heading to Japan to defend their titles at the Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup. The three-day event in Tokyo will be held between 31 October and 2 November. The 2023 World Deaf Rugby Sevens Cup in Argentina saw the men's team defeat Australia with a 20-5 victory sealing their second title in the sevens tournament and third consecutive title in the Deaf Rugby World Cup for the two Welsh sides. The women seven's tournament made its debut in 2023 with England beaten 32-0 in the final by Wales. At their final preparation session before leaving for Japan, players and staff came together at their training ground in Neath, and spoke to BBC Sport Wales. Wales Deaf eye World Cup as they take on Jamaica Wales deaf men and women crowned sevens champions The day ended with the presentation of the kit that both teams will be wearing in Tokyo. Sian-Elin Melbourne, chair of Wales Deaf Rugby, also shared a final message to the teams. "You are not just representing yourselves," said Melbourne. item.title: From end zone to sideline, Roger Bacon was always 'home' to Mike Blaut
item.description: As a little kid, Mike Blaut spent Roger Bacon football games playing backyard football in the end zone at what is now Bron Bacevich Memorial Stadium . Over four decades later, Blaut stood on the same field as the head coach of his alma mater, watching the final seconds tick away on a night that made school history. Roger Bacon won its first regional championship in 2020 , securing the program's first berth in the state Final Four. For Blaut, who graduated from Roger Bacon in 1988 and spent the majority of his coaching career there, the moment was more than a football milestone. It's also an accomplishment − winning a regional title at home − that will likely never happen again since regional playoff games were not held at neutral sites during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season. "Just the fact that I'm getting old. I've done it for so long," Blaut said. "I knew that I was on the back-9 of my career. I've been kicking it around and thinking maybe it was the right time. As the season was winding down, it became the right time for me to walk away." Blaut began his coaching career with the Spartans as a defensive backs coach in 1988 shortly after graduating, starting a journey that would take him to multiple other programs before returning to Roger Bacon. "I grew up there. I don't remember a time of not being there," Blaut said. "It is home. That's where my family has been. The hardest part is walking away from all of that." That connection helped shape the coach he became. Blaut learned the program's traditions under Ron Henke, a fellow Roger Bacon graduate who coached the Spartans with a mentality rooted in the school's identity. "Spartans never quit. After a brief stint at Northwest, Blaut returned to Roger Bacon in 1993. After coaching stops at Oak Hills and North College Hill, he came back to his alma mater again in 2008 as offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach. Becoming the head coach in 2015 fulfilled a longtime ambition. "That was my ultimate goal," Blaut said. "If I got it, great. I got the chance, so I took it." item.description: If you want to look at the Syracuse Orange football team with a glass half-empty point of view, you can simply point to the team's record. The Orange 3-4 entering play on Saturday afternoon against SMU. With a difficult end of season schedule, there's a very good chance that the Orange finish under .500 and miss a bowl game for the second straight year. If you want to look at the Orange from a glass half-full point of view, you can say that the Orange are 3-4, but they are developing young talent like Calvin Russell III. And they've had to navigate a very tenuous quarterback rotation that has seen each of its top-3 signal callers get injured at some point this season. Beyond that? The Orange could easily be 5-2 if they weren't struggling so bad in the special teams department. The Orange could have beaten Cal in Week 2, but were undone by missed kicks, and the same could be said for the Louisville game in Week 6. Notre Dame co-coach Madison Salkowski added: "It's very gratifying but we never take it for granted. Obviously there's a lot of tough competition in Region Nine. We know that. item.title: Blackhawks coach sounds off after Chicago takes ‘a step backward’ in loss to Red Wings
item.description: Chicago Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill did not hide his frustration after Thursday’s 4-1 loss to the Detroit Red Wings . He called the performance a major step backward, criticizing his players’ effort, skating and attention to detail. The Blackhawks entered the game looking to build consistency. Instead, they struggled defensively and allowed Detroit to control the game, despite captain Connor Bedard ‘s early goal. “ We had just way too many guys that wasn’t close, not enough good,” Blashill told NHL reporters. MORE: Blackhawks coach reveals why Connor Bedard stays on ice in big moments Final: Detroit 4, Chicago 1 — Chicago Blackhawks (@NHLBlackhawks) October 30, 2026 He acknowledged Chicago had previously lost games through critical mistakes despite playing reasonably well. “We’ve had a lot of games throughout this season where we did a lot of good things and maybe beat ourselves with critical mistakes, but for the most part throughout the game, we played pretty good hockey,” Blashill said. “Those are learning moments and you keep getting better.” However, Thursday’s performance offered little encouragement. “Tonight, to me, wasn’t that at all. It’s a step backwards,” Blashill said. “Because you just had too many guys that weren’t skating, didn’t compete hard enough, or not enough attention to detail. To me, tonight wasn’t close.” Blackhawks’ road struggles continue Chicago Blackhawks head coach Jeff Blashill (middle) talks with referee. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Red Wings’ Viktor Arvidsson delivered the decisive performance, recording his sixth career hat trick and adding an assist. Lucas Raymond also scored, while Alex DeBrincat contributed two assists. Bedard opened the scoring for Chicago at 5:59 of the first period. However, Arvidsson tied the game in the second before Raymond gave Detroit the lead early in the third. Arvidsson then added two more goals to complete his hat trick. John Gibson stopped 18 shots, including Frank Nazar’s second-period penalty shot. The defeat dropped Chicago to 0-5 on the road this season. Beat reporter Ben Pope described it as “ one of their worst efforts .” Meanwhile, Paul Bissonnette bluntly called the Blackhawks “pathetic.” The Blackhawks are pathetic. — Paul Bissonnette (@BizNasty2point0) October 30, 2026 Blashill’s criticism points toward a bigger concern than one disappointing result.
